summary: Ranolazine is an antianginal used for chronic angina, alone or with other agents. Unlike traditional antianginals, it relieves angina without clinically meaningful effects on heart rate or blood pressure, by inhibiting the cardiac late sodium current. It is a CYP3A4 substrate, prolongs the QT interval, and is contraindicated with strong CYP3A inhibitors and inducers and in liver cirrhosis.
indications: Treatment of chronic angina, used alone or in combination with beta-blockers, nitrates, calcium channel blockers, antiplatelet therapy, lipid-lowering therapy, ACE inhibitors, and angiotensin receptor blockers

dosage.d: Initial 500 mg twice daily; increase to 1000 mg twice daily based on symptoms
dosage.n: Max 1000 mg twice daily; swallow whole

dosage.c: With moderate CYP3A inhibitors (diltiazem, verapamil, erythromycin)
With strong CYP3A inhibitors or inducers

admin: Swallow the extended-release tablet whole; do not crush, break, or chew
Take with or without food, at about the same times each day
Limit to 500 mg twice daily when used with moderate CYP3A inhibitors
Avoid grapefruit juice and grapefruit products
Review concomitant QT-prolonging and CYP3A drugs before starting
moa: Ranolazine selectively inhibits the late phase of the inward sodium current (late INa) in ischemic cardiac myocytes. By reducing intracellular sodium accumulation, it limits sodium-dependent calcium overload, which decreases ventricular diastolic wall tension and myocardial oxygen consumption and improves myocardial perfusion. These antianginal and anti-ischemic effects occur without significant changes in heart rate or blood pressure; the exact mechanism of symptom relief is not fully established.

absolute: Concomitant use with strong CYP3A inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, clarithromycin, nelfinavir, ritonavir)
Concomitant use with CYP3A inducers (e.g., rifampin, phenobarbital, phenytoin, carbamazepine, St. John's wort)
relative: Conditions predisposing to QT prolongation / concomitant QT-prolonging drugs
monitor: Renal function and blood pressure (especially with renal disease)

preg: There are limited human data; animal studies show developmental effects at high doses. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: It is not known whether ranolazine is excreted in human milk; avoid breastfeeding or weigh the benefit against potential infant risk.
renal: Acute renal failure has occurred in some patients with severe renal impairment while taking ranolazine; blood pressure can rise in patients with renal impairment. Monitor renal function and avoid in severe renal impairment.
hepatic: Contraindicated in liver cirrhosis because hepatic impairment increases ranolazine concentrations and QT prolongation. Use caution in lesser hepatic dysfunction.

major: Strong CYP3A inhibitors and CYP3A inducers - contraindicated
QT-prolonging drugs (Class IA/III antiarrhythmics, some antipsychotics/antibiotics) - additive QT risk
Simvastatin and other CYP3A statins - ranolazine raises levels (limit simvastatin dose)
moderate: Moderate CYP3A inhibitors (diltiazem, verapamil, erythromycin) - limit ranolazine to 500 mg twice daily
P-glycoprotein inhibitors (e.g., cyclosporine) - increase ranolazine levels
Digoxin - ranolazine increases digoxin levels; adjust as needed
Metformin - ranolazine increases metformin exposure; limit metformin dose
minor: Drugs metabolized by CYP2D6 (e.g., tricyclic antidepressants - increased levels)
interactions.food: Take with or without food; avoid grapefruit juice (CYP3A inhibition).
interactions.diagnostics: Causes dose-related QT prolongation on ECG.

monitoring: ECG / QT interval, especially with QT-prolonging drugs
Renal function and blood pressure (particularly in renal impairment)
counsel: Swallow the tablet whole; do not crush, break, or chew
Tell your doctor about all other medicines - some are dangerous to combine with this drug
Report fainting, palpitations, or a very slow heartbeat
This medicine treats angina but does not relieve an acute angina attack - use your rescue nitroglycerin for that
pk: Antianginal effect over days at steady state
pearls: Relieves chronic angina WITHOUT lowering heart rate or blood pressure - useful when those limit other antianginals
Contraindicated with strong CYP3A inhibitors/inducers and in liver cirrhosis
Prolongs QT - avoid stacking with other QT-prolonging drugs
Raises digoxin and simvastatin levels - adjust those doses
missed: Take the missed dose at the next scheduled time; do not double the next dose to make up for a missed one.
overdose: Overdose may cause dizziness, nausea/vomiting, diplopia, paresthesia, confusion, syncope, and QT prolongation. There is no specific antidote; provide continuous ECG monitoring and supportive care. Ranolazine is highly protein-bound, so hemodialysis is unlikely to be effective.
